newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bankers to put up credit report system.
newsitem.headline: Manila bankers to put up credit report system.

text.p: The Bankers Association of the Philippines will establish a sophisticated credit report system in a bid to minimise risks in consumer loans, the group's executive director Leonilo Coronel told reporters late on Thursday.
"The consumer retail market, although there are some bad experiences, will be here to stay. That's why the BAP is looking at a way to minimise the risks," he said.

"We're going into a full-fledged credit reference group similar to what you see in developed markets," he said, adding that this will give a list of who not to lend to and the credit rating of borrowers.
Local banks had aggressively shifted to consumer lending through credit cards and car loans after being squeezed out from the high-end market by stiffer competition from foreign banks.
The high-end market catered to the top corporations in the country.
The Philippines allowed ten foreign banks to enter the market in 1995 to spur investments in the country.
Analysts had raised concerns on banks' consumer loans especially after a financial crisis hit a small thrift bank Monte de Piedad & Savings Bank.
"Banks are beginning to be careful about the so-called market share orientation," added BAP president Deogracias Vistan.
Some banks, in a bid to get a bigger market share in consumer lending, had been lax in their credit checks and emphasized on faster consumer loan approvals.
